propositions: A committed lock pins transitive dependencies, causing advisories on those pins to block all in-flight changes regardless of whether those changes touch the dependency map.
pip-audit cannot distinguish reachable from merely-present dependencies in the environment, so base-install scanning catches advisories from extra-only capping dependencies.

uv lock --upgrade-package is a no-op against an upstream cap; constraint-dependencies can only narrow existing constraints and returns UNSATISFIABLE as expected output, not proof that upgrade is impossible; override-dependencies is the correct instrument to replace a capped requirement.

The remediation order is: upgrade the direct dependency first; if an upstream cap blocks that, use override-dependencies with written justification naming the advisory, capping package, and safety rationale; then track the upstream fix.

Gerrit verify should block on an advisory only when the change touches the dependency map (uv.lock, pyproject.toml, etc.), not universally; the scheduled main lane should block releases and file/update a deduplicated ticket.

Advisory severity thresholds follow OSS convention: CRITICAL/HIGH fail the gate; MEDIUM warns; LOW is tracked; unrated advisories are treated as HIGH and fail; override-dependencies must carry a REMOVE-WHEN condition to enable detection of staleness.
